articles.body: NEW DELHI: The RSS has joined the campaign against “dimagi Naxals” which PM Modi launched on Aug 15, with its affiliated weekly ‘Organiser’ arguing that the Sonia Gandhi-led National Advisory Council (NAC) under UPA allowed Maoist-influenced thinking to enter policymaking.In an editorial, ‘Organiser’ termed NAC as marking the “classic takeover of the ‘dimagi Naxals’ of governance”. It said, “As the armed rebellion has failed miserably, the dimagi variant has taken charge.” The editorial added penetrating bureaucracy, policy machinery, legal system, academia, media and NGOs formed part of this “revolutionary strategy”.The weekly stopped short of accusing Sonia or Congress brass of links with Maoists, directing its criticism at NAC and the ideological influence the body brought into governance.It distinguishes “dimagi Naxals” from ordinary agitators or reform groups, acknowledging issues such as education and climate change can be genuine while alleging such concerns may be appropriated by an ideological core. In his I-Day speech, PM said armed Naxalism was nearing its end but people subscribing to the ideology who entered govt panels as advisers were still looking to create violence and anarchy.That reference also appeared to recall UPA-era controversies involving human rights activist Binayak Sen. Sen, arrested in 2007, was nominated to the Planning Commission steering committee on health in 2011.The govt has sought to draw a boundary around the expression. Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said Modi was not accusing opposition netas or parties, but referring to those supporting Maoists, who reject Constitution and back separatism.Set up in 2004 and chaired by Sonia Gandhi with cabinet-rank status, NAC brought activists, academics and experts into policymaking and played an important role in measures such as RTI and MGNREGA.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Bryan Kohberger seeks judge’s removal in escalating bid to undo guilty plea
articles.summary: Bryan Kohberger is seeking to withdraw his guilty plea for the murders of four University of Idaho students, arguing he was coerced into a false confession.
articles.body: Bryan Kohberger, the man convicted of fatally stabbing four University of Idaho students, is asking a court to disqualify the judge in his case and has asked for a change of venue as he attempts to take back his guilty plea. Motions for both requests were filed Thursday by Kohberger's new court-appointed attorney, Gregory Rauch. The move came after Kohberger was convicted of first-degree murder. Kohberger has since claimed he is innocent and has blamed his defense team for leading him to make a false confession. BRYAN KOHBERGER GETS NEW ATTORNEY APPOINTED AFTER HE ASKS COURT FOR POST-CONVICTION RELIEF IN IDAHO MURDERS The motions are asking for Fourth Judicial District Judge Steven Hippler to be disqualified for Kohberger's post-conviction court proceedings and for the hearings to be moved out of Ada County. The motion to disqualify Hippler questions his impartiality. "This motion does not rest upon one adverse ruling, one harsh statement, or the mere fact that the judge who presided over Bryan Kohberger’s criminal case has been assigned to his post-conviction proceeding," the motion states. "It rests upon the extraordinary convergence of all of them." Although his original criminal trial was relocated to Ada County in 2024 to ensure an impartial jury and adequate resources, his lawyers argue those concerns are irrelevant to a bench proceeding decided solely by a judge. BRYAN KOHBERGER'S POST-CONVICTION RELIEF BID ENABLED BY FLAWED PLEA DEAL, PSYCHOLOGIST ARGUES Kohberger, 31, last year pleaded guilty to four counts of first-degree murder and a felony burglary charge for the 2022 stabbing deaths of University of Idaho students Madison Mogen, 21, Kaylee Goncalves, 21, Xana Kernodle, 20, and Ethan Chapin, 20. However, Kohberger is now asking to be granted a trial even though he could possibly face the death penalty. The central pillar of the motion to remove the judge rests on the "constitutional adequacy" of the trial counsel's preparation. Defense lawyers argued the capital trial schedule made it impossible to review the massive amount of evidence in the case. The defense cautioned the court that forcing it to proceed to trial under those conditions threatened Kohberger’s constitutional right to effective representation. Hippler rejected the defense’s claims that it was unprepared for trial, accusing it of using the massive volume of discovery as a tactic for delay rather than a genuine concern. KOHBERGER DEFENSE TEAM SAYS IT IS 'APPALLED' BY FORMER EXPERT'S PUBLIC COMMENTS ABOUT IDAHO MURDERS CASE The motion also refers to Hippler's statement during sentencing in which he made pronouncements regarding Kohberger's ability to tell the truth. "Do we really believe, after all of this, he is capable of speaking the truth?" he said, according to the document. The judge also called Kohberger a "faceless coward" and the "the worst of the worst." "Those statements are fundamentally different from believing Kohberger committed terrible crimes or deserved severe punishment," the motion states. "They are forward-looking judgments about his credibility. And credibility may now be at the center of this proceeding." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The move to change the venue asks the court to relocate the proceeding from Ada County, where Kohberger pleaded guilty and was sentenced, to Latah County, where the murders occurred. "Transfer is warranted in a case like this where ‘the convenience of witnesses and the ends of justice would be promoted by the change,’" that motion states.

articles.title: Trump says he secured ‘majority US control’ of large slice of Venezuela’s oil reserves
articles.summary: President Trump said Friday evening that there will be “majority U.S. control” of a large swath of Venezuela’s oil reserves. “BREAKING NEWS: The United States of America has just entered into an Agreement with the Country of Venezuela on, THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY!” Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social. “At my…
articles.body:
President Trump said Friday evening that there will be “majority U.S. control” of a large swath of Venezuela’s oil reserves.

“BREAKING NEWS: The United States of America has just entered into an Agreement with the Country of Venezuela on, THE BIGGEST OIL DEAL IN WORLD HISTORY!” Trump wrote in a post on Truth Social .

“At my direction, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, working closely with Highly Respected Interim President of Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, and, through a partnership with private business, have secured majority U.S. control of more than 65 BILLION BARRELS of proven Oil Reserves in Venezuela, at no cost to the American Taxpayer,” he added.

The 65-billion-barrel figure represents about 21 percent of Venezuela’s total proven reserves, which amount to 303 billion barrels.

A U.S. official told The Hill via email that Rodriguez granted a private company that is a joint venture between the U.S. government and a private operator in Venezuela 100-year “concessions” for oil fields containing 63 billion barrels of proven reserves. The private operator was not named.

The U.S. official also said that the U.S. government will have more than half of the value of the new oil company. This value will be divided between equity ownership and guaranteed oil offtake.

The U.S. would get 55 percent “effective output” of the joint venture, according to the official. And, they said, the new company would have the second-largest proven oil reserve in the world, following only Saudi Aramco.

After the U.S. entered Venezuela and took its then-leader Nicolás Maduro, Trump has repeatedly emphasized his desire for their oil.

Meanwhile, the U.S.’s desire for oil has only grown since then, as the war in Iran has thrown a wrench into global supplies with volatility in the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil shipping chokepoint.

The war has driven up domestic fuel prices, and gasoline currently sits at about $4.09 cents per gallon on average, according to AAA .

Trump, in his Friday evening post, wrote that the deal “will substantially lower Gas Prices for all Americans, long into the future, while helping to continue to set Venezuela on a course toward Tremendous Success and Great Prosperity.”

However, simply taking control of Venezuela’s oil fields may not necessarily mean more oil will be produced immediately.

After the U.S. incursion into Venezuela earlier this year, experts told The Hill that producers who may want to pump Venezuelan oil could face significant hurdles including physically getting infrastructure set up.

articles.title: US judge rejects Trump’s bid to switch hush-money case to federal court
articles.summary: The US president has sought to overturn his criminal conviction for falsifying business records, citing immunity.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump has once again lost a bid to transfer his criminal hush-money case from state to federal court, in a bid to have his felony conviction dropped.

On Friday, Judge Alvin Hellerstein declined Trump’s petition for a third time, ruling that the president’s arguments were “neither new nor legally sufficient”.

Trump became the first US president to be convicted of a crime in 2024, when a New York City jury found him guilty of 34 counts of falsifying business records.

Prosecutors had argued that Trump attempted to conceal hush-money payments to the adult film star Stormy Daniels, to avoid negative attention during his 2016 presidential bid.

Trump, however, has maintained that his conviction should be tossed, given a 2024 Supreme Court decision expanding presidential immunity. But Hellerstein once again rejected that argument.

“Paying hush money to an adult film star or engaging in a cover-up of an embarrassment are not subsumed in presidential immunity,” Hellerstein wrote.

Trump’s lawyers have already announced they would appeal, denouncing Hellerstein’s judgement as “baseless and lawless”.

“President Trump will be filing a powerful appeal, and will continue defeating Democrat weaponization at every turn,” a statement from Trump’s team said.

The case centres on a $130,000 payment Trump allegedly made through his fixer, Michael Cohen, to buy Daniels’s silence, after she claimed she had an affair with the Republican leader while he was married. Trump has denied any sexual liaison with Daniels.

Falsifying business records in New York is normally a misdemeanour, but it can be charged as a felony when committed in service of another crime. In the hush-money case, prosecutors claimed Trump had sought to unlawfully influence the 2016 election, which he ultimately won.

The New York indictment was one of four Trump faced in 2023, between his two terms as president.

The other indictments concerned allegations that Trump illegally withheld classified documents and attempted to undermine the 2020 elections, which he lost. Those cases were ultimately dropped after Trump won re-election in 2024.

Of the four indictments, only the New York case reached trial. While the felony convictions made Trump eligible for incarceration or a fine, Judge Juan Merchan ultimately sentenced the Republican leader to an unconditional discharge.

That meant he would face no jail time, nor a financial penalty, but the convictions would remain on his records. The sentencing came on January 10, 2025, just days before Trump’s second inauguration.

Trump has appealed his conviction in the years since the trial, and simultaneously has attempted to move the case to federal court, where he likewise hopes he can toss the charges.

As part of his appeal, Trump’s legal team has cited a July 2024 ruling from the Supreme Court, expanding the concept of presidential immunity.

Previously, presidents were shielded from prosecution for actions taken within their constitutional mandate. The 2024 decision broadened that scope to give presidents “presumptive immunity” for anything that could be considered an “official act”, an undefined concept.

Trump’s lawyers argued that, since the hush-money case presented evidence from his first term as president, it falls under that immunity.

Hellerstein has previously rejected that argument. In November, however, the 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals ordered Hellerstein to reconsider the case in light of the Supreme Court’s decision.

The appeals court, however, did not instruct Hellerstein how he should rule. In Friday’s decision, Hellerstein rejected implications from the Trump team that he would simply certify the appeals court ruling.

“Federal district courts are not certifying clerks,” the judge wrote.

Hellerstein also addressed the Supreme Court’s decision, ruling that Trump’s actions with regard to Daniels were not “official acts” of the presidency, even if some were taken while he was in office.

“There is no way that discussions regarding hush money payments to cover up the President’s relations with Stormy Daniels could be an official act. An affair, or a cover-up of an affair, is not within the ‘outer perimeter’ of the President’s official responsibilities,” Hellerstein wrote.

articles.title: Trump announces ‘biggest oil deal in world history’ with Venezuela
articles.summary: US president says deal secures majority control of more than 65 billion barrels of proven oil reserves in Venezuela.
articles.body:
The United States has struck a deal with Caracas that would give them control of some 65 billion barrels of Venezuela’s proven oil reserves, President Donald Trump has announced, while reviving the OPEC nation’s battered energy industry.

In a post on Truth Social, Trump said the “historic transaction more than doubles American oil reserves” and “will substantially lower gas prices for all Americans”.

“At my direction, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, and Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, working closely with Highly Respected Interim President of Venezuela, Delcy Rodriguez, and, through a partnership with private business, have secured majority US control of more than 65 BILLION BARRELS of proven Oil Reserves in Venezuela, at no cost to the American Taxpayer,” Trump wrote.

Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez welcomed the deal, which is expected to bring about $209bn to the state’s treasury.

The announcement followed weeks of negotiations over an agreement that would give American companies long-term access to a group of Venezuelan oilfields and guarantee the resulting crude supply to the US.

Venezuelan officials are preparing to sign agreements next week granting new oil exploration and production rights to a number of companies, particularly US firms.

Sources previously told Reuters news agency that a lease model was under consideration, with fields potentially auctioned to US producers, but the arrangement could face legal and constitutional challenges in Venezuela, where the state retains control over core oil industry activities.

The new deal would represent a dramatic expansion of Washington’s role in Venezuela’s oil industry as the Trump administration seeks to revive the country’s production and secure more crude for US refineries. Venezuela holds the world’s largest proven oil reserves, but produces only 1.25 million barrels per day, far below its potential after years of underinvestment, mismanagement and sanctions.

Trump did not disclose the structure of the agreement, the fields or companies involved, nor how the US would exercise majority control over the reserves.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio described the agreement as a win for both countries, saying on X that it would secure stable, low-cost oil for the US and help lower petrol prices.

For Venezuela, Rubio said the deal would bring nearly $100bn in private investment, support thousands of high-paying jobs and help rebuild the country’s economy.

articles.summary: Nashville International Airport could soon be renamed after Tennessee icon Dolly Parton, the governor and airport announced Friday.
articles.body: Nashville International Airport could soon be renamed after Tennessee icon Dolly Parton, the governor and airport announced Friday. The beloved country legend and philanthropist, who hailed from rural Tennessee, died Tuesday at the age of 80. The airport and Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee announced the intent to name the airport in her honor to create “a lasting tribute to her indelible legacy and the generations of people she inspired across Tennessee and around the world,” they said in a news release. Lee spoke with Parton’s team about the proposal this week and they expressed “their appreciation,” the governor said. “Dolly Parton’s extraordinary life is forever woven into the fabric of our state,” Lee said. “From her rural mountain home in East Tennessee to global stages, Dolly carried the Volunteer Spirit with her. At a place where Tennessee welcomes the world, it is fitting that Nashville International Airport would bear the name of our state’s favorite daughter and greet travelers with the enduring legacy of Dolly’s music, generosity, faith, and kindness.” The proposal to rename the airport will be addressed at the Metro Nashville Airport Authority’s meeting Sept. 17. A petition to rename the airport in honor of Parton, which was started more than a year before her death, has over 160,000 signatures as of Friday night and also garnered responses in support from a Nashville City Council member and a Tennesseee state representative. The “Queen of Country” died surrounded by loved ones following a brief battle with cancer. Her death was felt across the nation and the world, and inspired heartfelt tributes from fans, celebrities and politicians alike. Known beyond her music for her extravagant blonde hairdos, Southern charm, wit, generosity and kindness, Parton was beloved by generations. She was also a keen businesswoman and devoted philanthropist, creating the Dollywood Foundation for property relief and educational programs in East Tennessee, as well as Imagination Library, which mails free books to children around the world.
